Start with the expanded examples. Open further examples for options and alternative R approaches.

ceil

Round up

Stata 

generate y = ceil(x)

R base 

mutate(data, y = ceiling(x))

Stata reference · R reference

clonevar

Copy a variable

Stata 

clonevar x2 = x

R dplyr 

mutate(data, x2 = x)

Differs from Stata mutate(x2 = x) copies the R vector and attributes, but does not reproduce all Stata clonevar characteristics and notes.

Stata reference · R reference

collapse

Replace the data with group means

Stata 

collapse (mean) x1 x2, by(group)

R dplyr 

summarise(data, across(c(x1, x2), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .by = group)

Differs from Stata Assign the result to replace the data, as collapse does: data <- summarise(...). summ(data, x1, x2, .by = group) shows a summary table instead. R retains missing grouping keys; Stata tabstat by() and tabulate summarize() exclude missing grouping categories unless requested. Check the intended grouping sample.

Stata reference · R reference

Different statistics for different variables

Stata 

collapse (count) n = x (sum) total = y, by(group)

R dplyr 

summarise(data, n = sum(!is.na(x)), total = sum(y, na.rm = TRUE), .by = group)

Stata reference · R reference

cond

One value if a condition holds, another if not

Stata 

generate y = cond(x > 0, 1, 0)

R dplyr 

mutate(data, y = if_else(x > 0, 1, 0))

Differs from Stata With missing x, Stata's cond() takes the first value (missing counts as large); if_else() returns NA. Stata numeric missing values compare larger than every finite number; R comparisons return NA. Handle missing values explicitly before applying the condition.

Stata reference · R reference

destring

Text to numbers

Stata 

destring str_x, generate(num_x)

R tidystata 

mutate(data, num_x = destring(str_x))

Differs from Stata Text that is not a number becomes NA with a warning, as with force. destring(str_x, ignore = "kg") removes those characters first, like ignore(), so "10 kg" gives 10. Invalid numeric text becomes NA with a warning here; Stata destring without force refuses conversion of a variable containing such text.

Stata reference · R reference

egen

Ten groups of about equal size

Stata 

egen bins = cut(x), group(10)

R tidystata 

mutate(data, bins = xtile(x, 10))

Differs from Stata egen cut(), group() has its own grouping rule; xtile() follows Stata's xtile, the usual command for quantile groups.

Stata reference · R reference

Mark the first row of each group

Stata 

egen first = tag(group)

R tidystata 

mutate(data, first = is_first(group))

Differs from Stata Gives TRUE/FALSE; rows with a missing group are FALSE, as in Stata, unless .missing = TRUE. The R result is logical TRUE/FALSE rather than numeric 1/0; use as.integer() when the stored type matters.

24 more examples and alternatives

Number the groups

Stata 

egen id = group(g1 g2)

R dplyr 

data |> group_by(g1, g2) |> mutate(id = cur_group_id()) |> ungroup()

Differs from Stata cur_group_id() also numbers groups with missing keys; egen group() excludes those rows without the missing option. String collation can change ID ordering.

Stata reference · R reference

Sample statistic as a new variable

Stata 

egen x_avg = mean(x)

R dplyr 

mutate(data, x_avg = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))

Differs from Stata R functions keep missing values unless na.rm = TRUE; Stata's egen ignores them. For an all-missing group mean(..., na.rm = TRUE) gives NaN; Stata egen mean() gives numeric missing. Normalize NaN if that distinction matters.

Stata reference · R reference

Group median

Stata 

bysort group: egen med = median(x)

R dplyr 

mutate(data, med = median(x, na.rm = TRUE), .by = group)

Stata reference · R reference

Group minimum

Stata 

bysort group: egen mn = min(x)

R dplyr 

dplyr::mutate(data, mn = if (all(is.na(x))) NA_real_ else min(x, na.rm = TRUE), .by = group)

Differs from Stata All-missing groups return NA without evaluating min() on an empty set. All-missing groups produce -Inf/Inf and a warning in R max/min with na.rm = TRUE; Stata egen max()/min() returns missing.

Stata reference · R reference

Group maximum

Stata 

bysort group: egen mx = max(x)

R dplyr 

dplyr::mutate(data, mx = if (all(is.na(x))) NA_real_ else max(x, na.rm = TRUE), .by = group)

Differs from Stata All-missing groups return NA without evaluating max() on an empty set. All-missing groups produce -Inf/Inf and a warning in R max/min with na.rm = TRUE; Stata egen max()/min() returns missing.

Group statistic as a new variable

Stata 

bysort group: egen x_avg = mean(x)

R dplyr 

mutate(data, x_avg = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), .by = group)

Differs from Stata For an all-missing group mean(..., na.rm = TRUE) gives NaN; Stata egen mean() gives numeric missing. Normalize NaN if that distinction matters.

Stata reference · R reference

Groups by given cutpoints

Stata 

egen bins = cut(x), at(0(10)100)

R base 

mutate(data, bins = cut(x, breaks = seq(0, 100, 10), right = FALSE))

Differs from Stata right = FALSE makes each interval include its lower cutpoint, as egen cut() does. cut_length(x, 10) instead splits the range into 10 equal widths. cut() returns a factor of interval labels; egen cut() stores numeric lower endpoints even when interval closure matches.

Stata reference · R reference

First observed value across variables

Stata 

egen first = rowfirst(x1-x5)

R dplyr 

mutate(data, first = coalesce(x1, x2, x3, x4, x5))

Stata reference · R reference

Join variables into one string

Stata 

egen id = concat(a b), punct(_)

R base 

mutate(data, id = paste(a, b, sep = "_"))

Differs from Stata paste() turns NA into the text "NA"; egen concat() follows Stata missing-value and numeric-display conventions.

Stata reference · R reference

Last observed value across variables

Stata 

egen last = rowlast(x1-x5)

R dplyr 

mutate(data, last = coalesce(x5, x4, x3, x2, x1))

Stata reference · R reference

Count how many variables equal a value

Stata 

egen n9 = anycount(x1-x5), values(9)

R dplyr 

mutate(data, n9 = rowSums(across(x1:x5, ~ .x %in% 9)))

Stata reference · R reference

Percentage of the total

Stata 

egen p = pc(x)

R tidystata 

mutate(data, p = pc(x))

Computes 100 * x / sum(x, na.rm = TRUE). pc(x, prop = TRUE) gives total shares on a proportion scale; dplyr::percent_rank(x) gives percentile ranks. pct() is removed; use pc().

Stata reference · R reference

Rank, with ties averaged

Stata 

egen r = rank(x)

R base 

mutate(data, r = rank(x, na.last = "keep"))

rank() gives tied values their average rank, like egen rank(); dplyr::min_rank() gives them the lowest.

Repeating sequence

Stata 

egen s = seq(), from(1) to(3)

R dplyr 

mutate(data, s = rep_len(1:3, n()))

Stata reference · R reference

Standardise a variable

Stata 

egen z = std(x)

R tidystata 

mutate(data, z = std(x))

Z-score: (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE), using the sample SD. Add .by = g for by g: egen.

floor

Round down

Stata 

generate y = floor(x)

R base 

mutate(data, y = floor(x))

Stata reference · R reference

format

Display numbers with two decimals

Stata 

format x %9.2f

R base 

mutate(data, x_text = sprintf("%.2f", x))

R stores the number unchanged and formats it only when printing, for example with round(x, 2) or sprintf().

Stata reference · R reference

generate

Create a variable

Stata 

generate x2 = x^2

R dplyr 

mutate(data, x2 = x^2)

Assign the result to keep it: data <- mutate(data, ...). R has no separate generate and replace.

8 more examples and alternatives

Number of rows

Stata 

generate N = _N

R dplyr 

mutate(data, N = n())

Add .by = group for the number of rows in each group, like bysort group: generate N = _N.

Stata reference · R reference

Row number

Stata 

generate n = _n

R dplyr 

mutate(data, n = row_number())

Stata reference · R reference

Days between two dates

Stata 

generate days = d2 - d1

R base 

mutate(data, days = as.numeric(d2 - d1))

Stata reference · R reference

Dummy variable from a condition

Stata 

generate dummy = (x1 == 1 & x2 == 2)

R dplyr 

dplyr::mutate(data, dummy = as.integer(x1 %in% 1 & x2 %in% 2))

Differs from Stata Stata numeric equality is false for missing operands; %in% keeps the dummy zero when either input is missing. The R result is logical TRUE/FALSE rather than numeric 1/0; use as.integer() when the stored type matters.

Stata reference · R reference

Value from the previous row

Stata 

generate lag_x = x[_n-1]

R dplyr 

mutate(data, lag_x = lag(x))

This shifts rows, like x[_n-1], and ignores gaps in time. See L. for panel lags.

Stata reference · R reference

Value from two rows ahead

Stata 

generate lead_x = x[_n+2]

R dplyr 

mutate(data, lead_x = lead(x, 2))

Stata reference · R reference

Create a variable under a condition

Stata 

generate x2 = x^2 if x > 0

R dplyr 

mutate(data, x2 = if_else(x > 0, x^2, NA))

In Stata missing is larger than any number, so x > 0 is true for missing x. In R the condition is NA and so is the result.

Stata reference · R reference

Create a variable for some rows

Stata 

generate x2 = x^2 in 11/20

R dplyr 

mutate(data, x2 = if_else(row_number() %in% 11:20, x^2, NA))

Stata reference · R reference

inlist

Whether x equals any listed value

Stata 

generate y = inlist(x, 1, 3, 5)

R base 

mutate(data, y = x %in% c(1, 3, 5))

Differs from Stata %in% gives FALSE for missing x, as inlist() does. R returns a logical indicator rather than the numeric 1/0 stored by Stata generate; use as.integer() if the stored type matters.

Stata reference · R reference

inrange

Whether x lies within a range

Stata 

generate y = inrange(x, 1, 5)

R dplyr 

mutate(data, y = between(x, 1, 5))

Differs from Stata between() returns NA for missing x, whereas Stata's inrange() returns 0.

Stata reference · R reference

ln

Natural logarithm

Stata 

generate y = ln(x)

R base 

mutate(data, y = log(x))

Differs from Stata log10() matches Stata's log10(). R's log(0) is -Inf rather than missing. R log(0) gives -Inf and a negative input gives NaN with a warning; Stata ln() gives numeric missing for these invalid inputs.

Stata reference · R reference

missing

Whether a value is missing

Stata 

generate m = missing(x)

R base 

mutate(data, m = is.na(x))

Differs from Stata R returns a logical indicator rather than the numeric 1/0 stored by Stata generate; use as.integer() if the stored type matters.

Stata reference · R reference

mvdecode

Turn missing-value codes into missing

Stata 

mvdecode x, mv(-9)

R tidystata 

mutate(data, x = mvdecode(x, -9))

mvdecode(x, c(-8, -9)) handles several codes, like mv(-8 -9).

Stata reference · R reference

mvencode

Turn missing values into a code

Stata 

mvencode x, mv(-9)

R tidystata 

mutate(data, x = mvencode(x, -9))

Stata reference · R reference

pctile

Quantile cutpoints

Stata 

pctile p = x, nquantiles(4)

R tidystata 

summ(data, x, .stat = c("p25", "median", "p75"))

Differs from Stata summ() uses Stata's percentile rule. quantile(x, type = 2) is close, but treats some whole positions, such as 100 * 0.3, as fractional. summ() returns percentile values in a summary table; pctile creates a dataset column containing the cutpoints.

Stata reference · R reference

recast

Change the storage type

Stata 

recast double x

R base 

mutate(data, x = as.double(x))

R chooses storage automatically, so there is no compress either.

Stata reference · R reference

recode

Recode ranges of values

Stata 

recode x (1/5 = 1) (6/10 = 2) (11/15 = 3) (else = .), generate(x3g)

R tidystata 

mutate(data, x3g = stata_recode(x, 1:5 ~ 1, 6:10 ~ 2, 11:15 ~ 3, .default = NA))

Values that match no condition become NA, like else = . in Stata. tidystata::stata_recode(x, 1:5 ~ 1, 6:10 ~ 2, 11:15 ~ 3, .default = NA) follows Stata's rules directly: 1:5 is a closed range including decimals, and without .default unmatched values are kept. car::recode() and, from dplyr 1.2.0, replace_values() are other options.

Stata reference · R reference

1 more examples and alternatives

Turn one code into missing

Stata 

recode x (9 = .)

R tidystata 

mutate(data, x = stata_recode(x, 9 ~ NA))

tidystata::stata_recode(x, 9 ~ NA) and mvdecode(x, 9) give the same result.
